# Tracking

Automated tracking has come a long way in recetn years, and there are a wealth of different tools - open-source, free, user-friendly - that can track 100's of individuals or manmy keypoints on individual animals. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(gt)

tibble::tribble(
  ~Type, ~Name, ~Description,
  
  # Centroid tracking
  "Centroid", "[idtracker.ai](https://idtracker.ai)", "Hundreds of individuals",
  "Centroid", "[TRex](https://trex.run)", "Better background segmentation, but higher complexity",
  "Centroid", "[AnimalTA](https://vchiara.eu/index.php/animalta)", NA,
  
  # Pose estimation
  "Pose estimation", "[SLEAP](https://sleap.ai)", NA,
  "Pose estimation", "[DeepLabCut](https://deeplabcut.org/)", NA,
  "Pose estimation", "[LightningPose](https://lightning-pose.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)", NA,

  # Segmentation
  "Segmentation", "[OCTRON](https://octron-tracking.github.io/)", NA,
  
) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Type") |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = c(Name)) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") |>
  cols_width(
    Type ~ pct(30),
    Name ~ pct(10),
    Description ~ pct(20)
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#c4dbf4ff"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "bottom", color = "#d3d3d3", weight = px(1)),
    locations = cells_body()
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = css(padding.left = "20px"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Type)
  ) |> 
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100),
    row_group.padding = px(10)
  )
```
